### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via bindAppArtifactHandlers (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d816eab584237726d2e342fbf2b17a24c00c12e` — the merge of head `5753938245d5000bbacd6287e086b4a5e2c01604` into base `e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d816eab584237726d2e342fbf2b17a24c00c12e && git checkout 7d816eab584237726d2e342fbf2b17a24c00c12e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b 5753938245d5000bbacd6287e086b4a5e2c01604 && git checkout -B drift-repro e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b && git merge --no-ff 5753938245d5000bbacd6287e086b4a5e2c01604

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The contract member — right.** `IObjectQLEngine.bindHooks` opts gain an optional `wrapHandler`: a function of `(handler, hook: Hook)` that returns a handler, where `handler` and the returned function are both functions of `(context: HookContext)` returning `unknown`; typed by `import type { Hook, HookContext } from '../data/hook.zod'`. Both types are spec-owned (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, the `z.input` types of `HookSchema` and `HookContextSchema`), so the import satisfies the file header's own predicate ("a type that MOVES into spec loses the excuse" for `unknown`). The evidence bar holds: it is an option on an existing member whose cross-package consumer through the slot is already in the tree (`bindAppArtifactHandlers`, `packages/runtime`). Narrowness: the binder hands a `HookHandler` (`(context: HookContext)` returning a `Promise` of `void` or `void`), assignable to the declared parameter; the `unknown` return is exactly what the binder does with it (an async adapter that awaits `wrapped(context)` and returns nothing, result discarded), and anything narrower would force a retype or a cast of the one wrap passed (`withInProcessHookTitle` returns a `Promise` of `unknown`). `hook: Hook` whole rather than a pick of `name`: the runtime reads only `hook.name`, but a wrap that reads `runAs` or `object` is a legitimate use of the same option. Judged right, not a widening past need.
2. **Implementers — right.** `git grep "implements IObjectQLEngine"` on the head: `ObjectQL` only (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:4437`). Its `bindHooks` opts carry `wrapHandler?: BindHooksOptions['wrapHandler']`, the same signature, spread into the binder's opts. The structural fakes typed against `bindHooks` (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-*.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin-authored-hooks.test.ts`'s `vi.fn()`) take fewer optional opts and stay assignable; `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`.
3. **TSDoc on the member — true of the code, with one loose phrase.** "Called once per hook, at bind": `resolveHandler` runs once per hook in `bindHooksToEngine`'s loop; the events-times-objects registration reuses the one `wrapped`; the binder pin asserts `wrappedFor` stays at 3 after two `triggerHooks` rounds. "Never applied to the handler `bodyRunner` builds from a `body`": the body branch of `resolveHandler` returns before `resolveInProcessHandler` is reached, so a hook carrying both `body` and `handler` binds its body and the wrap is never consulted (the same outcome the removed pre-wrap produced). "The engine awaits a handler and discards its return value": `triggerHooks` (`await entry.handler(context)`), `dispatchUnscopedMultiWriteHooks` (`await entry.handler(wholeOpCtx)`) and `wrapDeclarativeHook`'s `runWithTimeout` (`await handler(ctx)`, or a `Promise.resolve().then(...)` around `handler(ctx)` raced against the timer under `timeoutMs`) read no return. "What it returns is what the engine calls" is loose — the engine calls `wrapDeclarativeHook(hook, adapter)` — but the next sentence states the discard, and the returned function is the hook's handler in the position any resolved handler takes. Not misleading; no edit owed.
4. **Behaviour for existing callers — right; with no option the bind is byte-for-byte as before.** `resolveInProcessHandler` is the old tail of `resolveHandler` moved verbatim (the hunk is pure insertion above `const h = hook.handler;`). Without `wrapHandler`, `resolveHandler` returns that function unchanged (`if (!fn || typeof opts.wrapHandler !== 'function') return fn;`). The two other callers in the tree, `ObjectQLPlugin`'s binds at `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:3121` and `:3723` (`{ packageId: 'metadata-service' }`), pass no option. The control pin asserts a named and an inline handler are called with the engine's own context object (identity). With the option, the adapter is always async and resolves `undefined`: every call site awaits and discards, so a synchronous throw becomes a rejection at the same `await` and nothing observable moves. The wrap sits inside `wrapDeclarativeHook`, where the removed pre-wrap sat, so the `runAs` swap of `ctx.api` and the fire-and-forget `detached` view are read by the title view at call time as before. The `meta` registered with the engine is now the app's own declaration rather than the pre-wrap's copy; nothing in `packages/objectql/src` or `packages/runtime/src` reads `meta.handler`, and `wrapDeclarativeHook` reads only `async`, `runAs`, `name`, `condition`, `timeoutMs` and `onError`.
5. **The removed inline pre-wrap — every door it served is still served.** The base `hookWithInProcessTitle` wrapped a hook whose `handler` is a function; the head wraps that function and the function a string `handler` names (the bind's `functions`, then the same package's engine-registered function through the unchanged `ownPackageFunction`). Copy semantics hold more simply than before: the binder never writes the hook object, and PR #24356's runtime pin "the app's own declaration is not rewritten" (`expect(hook.handler).toBe(handler)`) is unchanged at head (blob `a45861e6a7`, equal to the merge base's) and green under `Test Core` (6 of 6 shards `success`). PR #24356's verify pin (`harness.hook-title-door.test.ts`, blob `9d9503a70e`) is likewise unchanged and green. `withInProcessHookTitle` and `buildTitleSurface` are untouched (`body-runner.ts` is not in the file list).
6. **The pins — they pin the changeset's claims, with a control.** `harness.named-hook-title-door.test.ts`: on both `bootStack` doors (artifact `runtimeModule` plus string `handler`; source `functions` plus a name) `ctx.title()` is `L1 · Widget`, `ctx.title('product')` is `Widget (W-1)`, `ctx.title('spare')` is `'null'` — the same `EXPECTED` PR #24356's pin holds for an inline handler and a `body`, which serves as the cross-file control. `hook-binder-wrap-handler.test.ts`: the three in-process kinds take the wrap once each at bind; a `body`'s handler never does; the control without `wrapHandler` is by context identity. Both files are compiled by their package's `tsconfig.test.json` (`src/**/*`, no test exclusion) behind `check:test-typecheck`. Not pinned, judged from code only: a hook carrying both `body` and `handler` under `wrapHandler` (item 3). The PR's before-reading on `ee882b845` (both named doors red with `TypeError: ctx.title is not a function`) is the dev's local measurement, taken as the PR's claim and consistent with the base code as read.
7. **Scope — right.** Seven files, +297 / -24, no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` `success`), head repo equal to base repo, no ADR governs `bindHooks` opts (the file's ADR anchor is on `transaction`, ADR-0067 and ADR-0119, untouched; `Lint & Repo Gates` `success` carries `check:adr-anchors`).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` — right. `IObjectQLEngine.bindHooks` opts gain an optional member: an additive widening of a published contract type. It matches the PR body's and the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, the retriage `6255696396` and the regrade `6255762317`.
- `@objectstack/runtime: patch` — right. `bindAppArtifactHandlers` changes behaviour and no published surface: its signature is unchanged and `withInProcessHookTitle` stays a module export off the package index.
- `@objectstack/objectql: patch` — **wrong, under-graded; FAIL item.** `BindHooksOptions` is published from the package index (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts:391`, `export type { BindHooksOptions, BindHooksResult }`) and gains the accepted key `wrapHandler`; `ObjectQL.bindHooks`, a method of the published class, accepts the same new key. That is "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface (a new exported symbol on an index, a new accepted key or value)", which the level rule the `Check Changeset` gate prints (the maintainer's ruling on decision batch #35) grades at least `minor`; the commit type `fix(` does not lower it. The gate's level axis stayed green because it requires only ONE moved package at `minor` or above (spec here), and its own text says it cannot read WHICH package received the widening. Remedy: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor` in `.changeset/24289-named-hook-handler-ctx-title.md`; no other line moves. Earlier option additions on `BindHooksOptions` in the objectql changelog predate the rule and are not precedent.
- No entry for `@objectstack/verify` — right. The package publishes `files: ['dist', 'README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md']` and the PR adds one `src/*.test.ts`, so nothing it publishes moves. The gate counts the changeset files added against the merge base (1, non-empty) and does not judge per-package coverage; `Check Changeset` is `success` on both of its runs for this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Item 2 not built (dev deviation 3, `needs_decision`) — accepted as the brief's own route.** `HookContextSchema` declares no `title` at head (grep over `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`), and the dispatch claim `6257131238` makes item 2 conditional on item 1 delivering at every in-process door. The options go to the maintainer through the seat; not judged here.
2. **Accuracy of the PR's own text — accurate.** The changeset's "Unchanged" paragraph and the PR body's P3 table name the doors that do and do not deliver `ctx.title`; the "no wrap passed" row for the metadata-service bind is confirmed (`plugin.ts:3121`, `:3723`), and no function is registered under the `metadata-service` owner anywhere in `packages/`. No sentence in the diff — the two TSDoc blocks, the runtime comment, the two test headers, the changeset — claims `ctx.title` on every door; each is scoped to the binder's option, to `bindAppArtifactHandlers`, or to the two `bootStack` doors. The docs (`skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`) stay untouched, as the claim's hold-off requires.
3. **No `@objectstack/verify` changeset (dev deviation 1, G4)** — answered in ②: right.
4. **`body-runner.ts` untouched; its `withInProcessHookTitle` "Why" docblock still speaks of the inline handler only (dev finding, carrier none)** — accepted as polish outside the claim's file surface (`body-runner.ts` only if the signature must change; it did not). Not a FAIL item; the next edit to that file owns the sentence.
5. **The contract file's header** still lists `HookContext` among the "packages/objectql-local" types the contract must spell as `unknown`, one screen above the import this PR adds. The header's own live predicate authorises the import; the stale example predates this PR. Polish, not blocking.
6. **Test wall time** — the verify pin boots two stacks under a 120 s per-test ceiling, the same shape as PR #24356's landed pin; not measured here, and `Test Core` is `success`. Nothing owed in this record.
7. **Dev deviations 2 and 5** (a detached primary checkout in the dev's own container; three prerequisite-refused gate families re-run to exit 0) — recorded, no contract bearing.
